question: Can ALTER ROLE increase the maximum number of simultaneous autovacuum workers for a user's future sessions?
expected_answer: No; autovacuum_max_workers is server-start-only and cannot be set with ALTER ROLE.

evidence_spans.quote: autovacuum_max_workers ( integer ) Specifies the maximum number of autovacuum processes (other than the autovacuum launcher) that may be running at any one time. The default is three. This parameter can only be set at server start.
Note that some settings cannot be changed after server start, and so cannot be set with these commands (or the ones listed below).

reasoning_chain: Identify autovacuum_max_workers as a server-start-only setting; apply the SQL configuration restriction to ALTER ROLE.

question: Which SQL command can establish a global default for a two-part extension option before its module is loaded?
expected_answer: ALTER SYSTEM; the option is accepted as a placeholder until its extension loads.

evidence_spans.quote: Because custom options may need to be set in processes that have not loaded the relevant extension module, PostgreSQL will accept a setting for any two-part parameter name. Such variables are treated as placeholders and have no function until the module that defines them is loaded.
The already-mentioned ALTER SYSTEM command provides an SQL-accessible means of changing global defaults; it is functionally equivalent to editing postgresql.conf .

reasoning_chain: Two-part unloaded-extension options can be set as placeholders; ALTER SYSTEM supplies the global-default SQL mechanism for such an option.

question: With plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan, will changing JIT cost limits just before execution revise the prepared plan's JIT decisions?
expected_answer: No; the generic plan uses the JIT cost settings from prepare time.

evidence_spans.quote: Custom plans are made afresh for each execution using its specific set of parameter values, while generic plans do not rely on the parameter values and can be re-used across executions. Thus, use of a generic plan saves planning time, but if the ideal plan depends strongly on the parameter values then a generic plan may be inefficient. The choice between these options is normally made automatically, but it can be overridden with plan_cache_mode . The allowed values are auto (the default), force_custom_plan and force_generic_plan .

These cost-based decisions will be made at plan time, not execution time. This means that when prepared statements are in use, and a generic plan is used (see ), the values of the configuration parameters in effect at prepare time control the decisions, not the settings at execution time.

reasoning_chain: force_generic_plan selects a reusable generic plan; generic-plan JIT decisions are controlled by prepare-time settings.

question: When must I lower the cost setting for JIT function inlining to affect a prepared generic plan?
expected_answer: Lower jit_inline_above_cost at prepare time, rather than just at execution time.

evidence_spans.quote: jit_inline_above_cost ( floating point ) Sets the query cost above which JIT compilation attempts to inline functions and operators.

These cost-based decisions will be made at plan time, not execution time. This means that when prepared statements are in use, and a generic plan is used (see ), the values of the configuration parameters in effect at prepare time control the decisions, not the settings at execution time.

reasoning_chain: Resolve inlining behavior to jit_inline_above_cost; apply the prepare-time rule to that identified cost setting.

question: Why might setting jit_above_cost to zero be counterproductive for a workload of short queries?
expected_answer: It makes positive-cost queries eligible for JIT, whose compilation overhead often exceeds the savings for short queries.

evidence_spans.quote: jit_above_cost ( floating point ) Sets the query cost above which JIT compilation is activated, if enabled (see ). Performing JIT costs planning time but can accelerate query execution.

JIT compilation is beneficial primarily for long-running CPU-bound queries. Frequently these will be analytical queries. For short queries the added overhead of performing JIT compilation will often be higher than the time it can save.

reasoning_chain: A zero threshold admits positive-cost short queries; their typical compilation overhead makes that policy counterproductive.

question: Does a pg_default_acl entry with defaclobjtype = f and defaclnamespace = 0 replace the hard-wired default function privileges?
expected_answer: Yes; f means function, and the global entry overrides hard-wired defaults.

evidence_spans.quote: defaclobjtype char Type of object this entry is for: r = relation (table, view), S = sequence, f = function, T = type, n = schema

There are currently two types of entry: global entries with defaclnamespace = zero, and per-schema entries that reference a particular schema. If a global entry is present then it overrides the normal hard-wired default privileges for the object type.

reasoning_chain: Decode f as a function ACL entry; interpret namespace zero as global and apply its override semantics.

question: Will changing a pg_default_acl entry with defaclobjtype = S change privileges on sequences that already exist?
expected_answer: No; S denotes sequences, and pg_default_acl is consulted only during object creation.

evidence_spans.quote: defaclobjtype char Type of object this entry is for: r = relation (table, view), S = sequence, f = function, T = type, n = schema
pg_default_acl is only consulted during object creation.

reasoning_chain: Map S to sequences; the creation-only consultation rule excludes changes to existing sequence privileges.

question: How can I obtain a descriptor-based read position beyond 2GB when I start with a large object's OID?
expected_answer: Open the OID with lo_open, then call lo_tell64 on the returned descriptor within that transaction.

evidence_spans.quote: The lobjId argument specifies the OID of the large object to open. The mode bits control whether the object is opened for reading ( INV_READ ), writing ( INV_WRITE ), or both. (These symbolic constants are defined in the header file libpq/libpq-fs.h .) lo_open returns a (non-negative) large object descriptor for later use in lo_read , lo_write , lo_lseek , lo_lseek64 , lo_tell , lo_tell64 , lo_truncate , lo_truncate64 , and lo_close . The descriptor is only valid for the duration of the current transaction.
Note that lo_tell will fail if the current read/write location is greater than 2GB. lo_tell64 is new as of PostgreSQL 9.3.

reasoning_chain: Convert the OID to the required descriptor with lo_open; choose lo_tell64 because lo_tell cannot report that position.

question: What will an INV_READ large-object descriptor return from an unallocated gap if another transaction writes into that gap after its opening snapshot?
expected_answer: Zeroes for the gap preceding the last existing chunk; the later write is not visible through that descriptor's snapshot.

evidence_spans.quote: with INV_READ you cannot write on the descriptor, and the data read from it will reflect the contents of the large object at the time of the transaction snapshot that was active when lo_open was executed, regardless of later writes by this or other transactions.
A read operation will, however, read out zeroes for any unallocated locations preceding the last existing chunk.

reasoning_chain: INV_READ preserves the opening snapshot despite later writes; sparse gaps in that snapshot produce zeroes.

question: What SQL expression reads the first three bytes using the identifier returned by a successful client-side large-object import?
expected_answer: lo_get(imported_oid, 0, 3), where imported_oid is the returned large-object OID.

evidence_spans.quote: The return value is the OID that was assigned to the new large object, or InvalidOid (zero) on failure.
lo_get ( loid oid , offset bigint, length integer ) bytea Extracts the large object's contents, or a substring thereof. lo_get(24528, 0, 3) \xffaaff

reasoning_chain: Successful import returns an OID; feed that OID to the SQL lo_get function with offset zero and length three.

question: Does enabling postgres_fdw parallel_commit make successive remote scans in a READ COMMITTED local transaction see different snapshots?
expected_answer: No; parallel_commit affects committing, while the remote transaction still uses REPEATABLE READ and a consistent snapshot.

evidence_spans.quote: parallel_commit ( boolean ) This option controls whether postgres_fdw commits in parallel remote transactions opened on a foreign server in a local transaction when the local transaction is committed.

The remote transaction uses SERIALIZABLE isolation level when the local transaction has SERIALIZABLE isolation level; otherwise it uses REPEATABLE READ isolation level. This choice ensures that if a query performs multiple table scans on the remote server, it will get snapshot-consistent results for all the scans.

reasoning_chain: parallel_commit changes commit scheduling, not scan isolation; the remote REPEATABLE READ rule preserves snapshot consistency.

question: Which separator does dynamic_library_path use between directory paths on Windows?

question: What is the default planning-effort level for the genetic query optimizer?

question: Which setting forces safe queries into parallel mode for testing in PostgreSQL 15?
evidence_quote: force_parallel_mode ( enum ) Allows the use of parallel queries for testing purposes even in cases where no performance benefit is expected. The allowed values of force_parallel_mode are off (use parallel mode only when it is expected to improve performance), on (force parallel query for all queries for which it is thought to be safe), and regress (like on , but with additional behavior changes as explained below).
